Hi Emily & Tom — thanks again for the live demo earlier today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we stay aligned: 

1) Volume profile (you said):
   - Steady-state: ~100M tokens / month across our summarization + search pipelines
   - Spiky peaks: up to ~160M in month-end reporting windows

2) Key constraints you called out:
   - Target unit cost somewhere between $18–$25 per 1M tokens
   - Need SOC2 / data isolation details before procurement sign-off
   - Preference for a committed reserved option if pricing gets into target band

3) Immediate asks from your side:
   - Confirm if the $18–$25 / 1M target is a hard ceiling or a goal range
   - If possible, share any incumbent pricing (OpenAI/Anthropic) you are comparing against

Next steps we suggested: I'll send a short mutual action plan and a pilot proposal that includes 100M/month baseline pricing and a reserved capacity option. Attached the MAP + demo recording for reference.

[Attachment: MedSift-MAP-v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]
[Attachment: demo-recording.mp4 (MP4, 28MB)]

Would you be able to confirm the final budget range by end of week so we can model committed discounts? If you prefer, we can also run a 2–4 week pilot at an interim rate to validate latency/cost before a longer commit.

Thanks — Aisha

Thanks Aisha — appreciate the recap and the recording. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volume: yes, ~100M tokens/month is our planning baseline. We typically provision to an 1.6x headroom for peaks, but our procurement team wants committed baseline numbers.
- Budget: the $18–$25 / 1M is the internal goal range. $18 is aspirational; $22–$25 is the expected realistic ceiling unless there are strong TCO justifications for higher.
- Incumbents: we are actively evaluating OpenAI (gpt-family pricing) and Anthropic (Claude) and a couple of managed open-model hosts. Our rough current blended cost sits around $28/1M after network + embedding preprocessing overheads.

Procurement asked for: a short procurement checklist (we attached the vendor intake spreadsheet) and an example reserved capacity term sheet if you have one. Also need SOC2 evidence and a sketch of data handling controls (KV cache / ephemeral logs).

Quick answers: a pilot at an interim rate to validate end-to-end latency and token accounting would be very welcome. Please include a target $/1M for both pilot and committed baseline in the MAP.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Reed
Head of Data Platform, MedSift
tom.reed@medsift.com

Thanks for the ping — quick benchmark note and recommended next step below. I kept this internal so we can refine before sending Tom.

Summary assumptions:
- Baseline volume: 100M tokens / mo (steady) with 1.6x peak headroom
- Token accounting: we assume 1 token ~= 4 characters typical for summaries (conservative)
- Pilot period: 2–4 weeks, accounted at a slight premium (we recommend pilot pricing = committed rate + 20%)

Preliminary unit-price comparison (all $ per 1M tokens):
- Redwood (hosted, standard quant/profile): $16 / 1M (100M committed)
- Redwood (reserved/dedicated pool, 12-month commit): $12 / 1M (100M/mo commit)
- OpenAI (public pricing blended after network & embedding costs): ~ $24 / 1M (client reported blended)
- Anthropic (estimated blended, enterprise terms): ~ $22–$26 / 1M
- Managed open-model hosts (self-hosted inference marketplaces): wide range, typically $8–$20 / 1M but with additional ops/security premium and variable latency

Initial read: we can comfortably propose a committed rate of $12–$14 / 1M for a 12-month 100M/mo reserved contract and still maintain target margin (Priyom — please validate GPU cost math per your model). If Tom wants faster time-to-value without a 12-month commit, propose a 4-week pilot at $18 / 1M (pilot = committed + 20% cushion). That matches their aspirational $18 while giving us room to show value and then move to $12 locked-in for a commit.

Next steps before sending to Tom: 
1) Priyom to confirm gross margin at $12 / 1M for 100M/mo commit (include sensitivity to +/-10% usage).
2) Aisha to prepare a one-page comparison (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic) that highlights latency SLOs, security posture (SOC2/KMS/HSM options), and the reserved capacity term sheet.
3) If positive, propose a pilot start date and a 12-month reserved term sheet (attach standard terms) in the MAP.

Ben Carter
Director, Solutions & GTM Economics, Redwood Inference
